question: The broker was validated as a broker (artifacts/11/gpu-broker-validation.json), on bare processes. What had never run is the path an actual job takes: the sandbox's own ./evaluate, inside amdpilot/solbench-job:2, with the container holding no GPU allocation of its own and leasing a card per measurement.

setup.note_on_visible_devices: The brokerless default from fleet.sh. GPU 0 is not in it: the authoritative scorer was re-timing gpt56-40 on GPU 0 throughout this test, which is exactly the arrangement the default exists to protect.
setup.kernel: the gpt56-40 agent's kernel for that problem

reading: Two clients were served at once because there were two cards, and two waited about 10.5 s -- one evaluation -- which is the broker doing its job rather than a failure. All four measured the same kernel to within 0.8%, which is the property that matters: a queued measurement is not a degraded one. The unbrokered control in the earlier artifact, four processes on one card, disagreed by up to 2.14x.
caveats: One problem, one kernel, four clients. This validates the plumbing end to end; it is not a re-measurement of contention at scale.

The wait recorded here is the broker's queue only. It is charged to the agent's own 3600 s session budget, which is why the projection in artifacts/11/concurrency-projection.json treats wait as a cost and not just as latency.
The containers were launched by hand with the same flags fleet.sh sets, not by the job daemon. The daemon's own argv is asserted separately in job-daemon's test_launch.py.
